name: Recharge Desk
office_task: Each month, turn the software we pay for on clients' behalf into one draft recharge invoice per client in Xero at our recharge prices, and hold it for a named person to release.
systems_of_record: the practice's subscription register (a sheet or the practice management system) that holds one recharge period per client per month, with each subscription on it reconciled to the supplier's bill, and issues the period's id (carried as job_id)

emits.write: One draft invoice in Xero per client per month, referenced job:<period id> (and the stage under a fixed-fee onboarding agreement), every line one of that client's subscriptions for the month with its register line reference in the notes, every price read from the recharge price list at draft time, and the client's signed approval attached for a seat or upgrade added mid-month. A second close of the same month updates the same draft.
emits.readback: Xero returns the InvoiceID; GET /api.xro/2.0/Invoices/{InvoiceID} must return the invoice with Reference job:<period id>, and that id is stamped on the period as seam.invoice_id. No id back is not a write: it raises invoice.write_failed and the run stops.

emits.write: The invoice leaves only after a release naming the practice manager, or naming the rule the partner set and showing the total is under its threshold; the release and the send time are recorded against the period.
emits.readback: GET /api.xro/2.0/Invoices/{InvoiceID} returns it AUTHORISED and sent to the contact, and the period read by its id shows seam.released_by (a person or a rule) before the send time. A send with no release on the record is refused.

emits.write: A parked or waiting invoice as an exception on the recharge period: the reason from the standard's fixed list (not_in_pricebook, unsigned_variation, write_failed) or over_threshold, the period id, the invoice id, the codes left unpriced, and exception_owner set to the person the practice named for recharges.
emits.readback: The exception desk returns an exception_id, and reading it back returns the job_id, the invoice_id, the reason and the exception_owner; the next run reads it there and stops until exception.closed.
